messages:
anna: Heads-up: saw a host-side perf regression on canary for tokenization path. p99 decode + parse jumped ~120ms after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak.

sam: ack. which tweak? the auto kernel picker change?

anna: yep. we changed heuristics to favor large-block kernels earlier. Perf trace showed extra copy in host parse when chunking small frames.

drew: can you paste the perf snippet?

anna: sure:
```
writev syscall count per request: before=2 now=8
avg small write size: 64 bytes
kv-cache lookup time unchanged
user CPU++ on proto-unpack
```

maria: that extra writev explains gRPC tail latency. small writes hit TCP/Nagle + http2 framing -> stalls

sam: i suspected fragmentation. did the runtime start emitting smaller proto messages due to the batching hint change?

anna: yes — autobatcher split earlier to favor larger kernels, but host preproc now slices more aggressively leading to many tiny frames.

drew: quick fix idea: coalesce adjacent small writes on host proxy before calling writev. Also add a batching threshold for proto emit (>=128 bytes) to avoid microwrites.

sam: can we test in canary? i can patch host-proxy with a naive coalesce for now.

anna: please. also add a perf counter: small_write_count and coalesced_bytes.

ci-bot: deploy started: canary/host-proxy-coalesce-PR#412 -> us-west-2 (canary)

maria: ran end-to-end: p50 unchanged, p95 -15ms, p99 -110ms on streaming endpoints. writev count dropped from 8->3. :tada:

drew: nice. create follow-up to tune kernel-selection heuristics so preproc doesn't over-slice. file an issue and tag runtime/ingress.

anna: filing now. Issue: https://rwd/issue/INF-8920

sam: thanks team. i'll keep an eye on related telemetry for the next 48h.

maria: note: also saw a small increase in request assembly CPU (2%), but net latency win worth it.

anna: closing loop: will add a unit test for proto coalesce and a canary metric alert if small_write_count spikes. :thumbsup:
